universal_lens: End-to-end 3D multi-object tracking unifies detection and data association via multi-modal fusion, eliminating sequential TBD paradigms. A unified mathematical framework integrating detection and tracking through joint optimization of temporal and spatial modalities.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference models trajectory confidence and state transitions using historical features for robust 3D MOT under uncertainty. Bayesian probabilistic inference over multi-modal sensor data enables conformal uncertainty quantification in motion estimation.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning maps sensor fusion and state transitions through dynamic trajectory prediction and confidence-guided NMS for autonomous driving. Situation-aware state transitions driven by historical feature fusion and 3D trajectory regression for dynamic environment modeling.

primitives.name: Integrated Detection and Tracking Framework
primitives.verbatim_quote: In this paper, a new end-to-end multi-object tracking framework is proposed, which integrates object detection and multi-object tracking into a single model.
primitives.assumptions: Detection and tracking are modeled as a unified optimization problem; no separate data association step required.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When sensor modalities fail or data is ambiguous, tracking performance degrades due to lack of explicit data association.

reasoning_traces.think: This chapter introduces YONTD-MOT, a novel end-to-end 3D multi-object tracking framework that merges detection and tracking into a single model. It challenges the classical tracking-by-detection (TBD) paradigm by removing the need for explicit data association modules. The approach leverages both 2D and 3D detectors, fusing their outputs early in the pipeline to enable robust tracking without requiring additional training. A key innovation lies in incorporating historical trajectory information to predict object states—specifically distinguishing between weak and strong objects—and guiding confidence-based non-maximum suppression. This enhances tracking stability and reduces false positives. Furthermore, the use of historical features boosts detector performance by capturing occlusion and disappearance behaviors more accurately. The framework is evaluated on standard benchmarks like KITTI and Waymo, demonstrating superior performance over existing TBD-based methods. The theoretical foundation rests on integrating probabilistic reasoning with geometric constraints from sensor data, enabling a unified treatment of perception and decision-making in autonomous systems.
